notes.title: Park Studio Beta 1.0 Development Update #1
notes.content:
Hello dear enthusiasts!

I'm Azael, the developer of Park Studio.



Today, I would like to share with you all everything I've been working on the past few months for the upcoming Beta update.


What is Beta 1.0?


Early this year, I announced that the next update would be Beta 1.0, but I didn't really explain what its goal was or what would be in it.



So, Beta 1.0 will be a complete rewrite of the game from the ground up, this was done in order to be more performant, and ensure quality and stability.

The update will bring back all Alpha features, this includes the building features, coaster features, landscape features, as well as some previously removed features such as Undo & Redo.

On top of that, Beta 1.0 will also introduce new features, more content and some great improvements to existing features. I won't share everything today, but look forward to more coaster types, new special tracks like switch tracks and turn tables and some major improvements to the coaster features.


Development Update


Let's now take a look at everything I've been working on, everything that you'll see below is still work in progress and subject to change.


Main Menu Redesign

Design & Navigation


The main menu was redesigned, it is now back to the left side similarly to Alpha 0.1. The new design is more visually pleasing and easier to navigate.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/2ae51613d4f2d2640563e6250ad45a36de59d301.png"]New Main Menu UI and background.



The background has also been reworked (WIP), and it will be updated as the game gets new features. The background will also have seasonal additions based on upcoming events or seasons like Halloween.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/v7ajjzz.gif"]Main Menu navigation, easier than ever.


New Settings


New settings were added, especially new graphics settings, these new settings were added to support a wider range of hardware with more fine-tuning to get the best looking game while keeping framerate high.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/GLN09Ol.gif"]New graphics settings.


Graphics Update


Speaking of graphics, the entire game's lighting and post processing has been redone to follow a Physically Based Lighting approach, which means Park Studio aims to simulate photo-realism.



The recent graphics improvements (WIP) were showcased in a recent video, you can watch it on the YouTube channel.


[previewyoutube="NUKxwYCX4G8;full"][/previewyoutube]

Performance Upgrade


Beta 1.0 will be far more optimized than the Alpha, ensuring a smooth 60 fps on the High settings, no matter the size or amount of content in your park, with minimal quality losses.



The update will also boost the Epic settings for image quality and stability, so it will be recommended to use Frame Generation, as the game only targets 45 fps on the Epic settings.


In-Game UI Redesign


Similarly to the Main Menu redesign, the in-game UI has also been refreshed, following the same consistent design and ease of navigation.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/73dafec2dea4c7ba13a6e05bdea1cdc8b881ae43.png"]In-Game UI on a flat map.



The redesign uses a similar layout and philosophy to Alpha 0.2. The goal is to have a maximum of free space in your view, so that the UI doesn't get in your way.



You might notice some pretty interesting changes to the UI, starting at the top left, there are two new buttons compared to the Alpha, these are the Photo Mode tool and Camera Modes.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/a1e0a18ebdc34143f8d94c49a419ccfa9d9780e2.png"]

The Photo Mode won't be part of the initial Beta 1.0 release, but it will come soon after, while the Camera Modes button will allow you to switch between the camera modes, these include: Drone, Walk and a brand new camera mode: Orbit.

The Orbit camera was a very requested feature, and I'm happy to announce that it will be added to Beta 1.0.



Then, at the top of the screen, there is a brand new UI element that I called the "Controls Bar"

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/487502efd0a613818f72bc8f374c29b1cb86652d.png"]

The "Controls Bar" is a dynamic UI element that will show you a list of controls that you can use, it will update as you navigate different menus or do different actions to show you exactly what shortcuts are available to you.

The "Controls Bar" can be disabled in the settings, if you don't want to see it.



Finally, at the bottom of the screen are your classic park controls and building buttons.


Park Management
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/dd0f5181f52a902420b6ecb9c1a20f331eebaf88.png"]

WIP Park Management Menu.



Park Management will be a feature available in the future, this is just an early design iteration for that menu, nothing here is functional except changing the name of your park.


Time & Weather
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/38608eab7bd800f6feae856ae1fa6ca41b578330.png"]

WIP Time & Weather Menu.



A brand new Time and Weather Menu was added, in order to give you control over the time of day, the weather and simulation speed all in one place.



You might notice a couple of new features, such as temperature, the calendar, seasons and the weather forecast.

All of these features are still work in progress and will be discussed in future devlogs, but for now I can reveal some information.

The temperature will affect your visitors and the ability for your rides to operate, the weather forecast will give you tips to ensure your visitor's happiness in all kinds of weather and the calendar will allow you to setup custom events such as celebrations, seasonal events or sales.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/00a8ae37de1d28e68797d4ea6e13d16264264bdb.png"]

Example of weather forecast tips.


Building Features Improvements


The Building features of Park Studio were massively improved, starting with the core: Selecting pieces.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/YCZbWHn.gif"]Improved way to select pieces in Beta 1.0.



As you can see on the gif above, selecting pieces is now very different compared to what it was in Alpha 0.2. Where Park Studio previously followed the common trend of the game genre, it now innovates with a more efficient and user-friendly way of selecting pieces and materials.



In Beta 1.0, some of the pieces will have families, and once you click on a "parent" of that family, it will open all of the pieces from that family, avoiding an unending list of pieces in a cluttered menu.



Materials were separated from the pieces entirely, where before you had 21 times every piece, you now only have one family of blank pieces, on which you can apply any material you want in one click.



Another major change is that the Scenery and Building pieces will now be merged in one single menu, with new filters and tags to search exactly the piece you want very quickly and easily.


Improved Building Controls


The controls were improved, where before you had to use your mouse wheel to move pieces up and down or rotate them, you will now be able to move your mouse on the screen in the direction you want the piece to go or rotate.



More improvements to the controls are coming as well as some new features to make building easier!


Introducing: the Spline Tools


The first brand new tool to join the Beta 1.0 toolset: the Spline Tools!



The spline tools are coming as a replacement and extension to the Path Tool. With the Spline Tools, you will be able to draw fences, paths, curbs, coaster supports and more.



This tool is still heavily work in progress, but here is a first look at how you'll be able to draw a fence that sticks to the terrain with ease.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/IiXKXiz.gif"]Spline Tools in action, drawing a fence on uneven terrain in a few clicks.


Major Terrain Improvements


The Terrain features of Park Studio were drastically improved, with improved visuals, faster sculpting and material painting and new features.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/f1782556c7711f959693749ad200be899c259470.png"]Improved terrain visuals with better transitions between grass and rock.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/bda698514bd622e192e455eea1921cc6d2592670.png"]New: displacement on terrain, adding real 3D detail to the surfaces.


Introducing: Terrain Stamps


Another brand new tool unique to Park Studio: Terrain Stamps!



Terrain Stamps work similar to pieces, but for your terrain! You might notice on the screenshot above that the terrain has very fine shapes, these were made with Terrain Stamps, combined with sculpting.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/n9GatF7.gif"]Terrain Stamps in action, placing shapes in one click.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/P926oVi.gif"]Moving stamps even after they are placed.



Terrain Stamps can be sculpted and painted over, making them your best friends for all your landscaping needs!


New Painting Features


Beta 1.0 will introduce three new painting features on top of simply painting materials: Painting Puddles, Wetness and Color!



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/YZVyTCW.gif"]Painting materials.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/8Jm58VW.gif"]Painting colors, puddles and wetness.


The Future


This concludes everything I've been working on the last few months! While it is a lot of work and improvements, this merely scratches the surface of what I plan to release in Beta 1.0, as a little gift, let me share with you the first part of the brand new timeline!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983429/a7c9405a0f2a97e3a6b3693661c47e8b9570d0db.png"]

I still have a lot of work to do, the next steps are the new coaster builder, with improved features and new coaster types, and adding building and scenery pieces.



Thank you so much for reading, I truly hope this extensive development update satisfies you all!



A quick reminder that if you'd like to support the project, there is a Patreon available, it doesn't offer anything just yet but after Beta 1.0, you will get access to early builds and exclusive looks at upcoming features! The Patreon is the best way to support me and the project.



Stay tuned as more will be revealed in the near future, as I keep making progress developing Park Studio's biggest update yet!

notes.title: Our Plans for 2025: Welcome to Beta 1.0
notes.content:
Happy New Year!

We hope you all had fun celebrating the end of 2024 and we wish you all the best for 2025!

This year, we have big plans for Park Studio, and it's time to reveal it all!

Welcome to Beta 1.0

The biggest thing coming in 2025 is the very first Beta release of the game, this massive update will extend Park Studio's feature set drastically and provide a first taste of the real ultimate Theme Park building and simulation game!

Beta 1.0 will be worked on throughout 2025 and will hopefully release by December this year or later in Early 2026.

As we revealed before, there will be Experimental releases during the development of the Beta, but the plans have changed:

- Instead of releasing the experimental builds on a separate branch, we will release the builds on the current main branch, overriding the current Alpha.

- Saving will still be enabled, even if you are not a Patreon supporter.

- The builds will only be released once enough content has been added and properly tested, meaning there might be only one release every quarter.

- Patreon supporters will get access to every functional builds, these builds are untested and may not add anything major however.

We will release the first Experimental build once all the currently available features in Alpha 0.2 are implemented in the Beta.

Regarding the price increase:

Park Studio's price will be increased to USD 19.99$ starting with the first Experimental Beta release. This is necessary to fund the future of the project and we hope you understand our decision, if you have already purchased Park Studio, this price increase won't affect you.

The price will be increased further in the future as Park Studio becomes more feature rich, we currently don't have a number to give as the price will depend on many variables that we cannot control, we will share the necessary information in due time.

Support us on Patreon!

If you'd like to get access to exclusive teasers and ultra-experimental builds then head over to our Patreon, your support helps us speed up Park Studio's development!

A look at our plans:

To end this announcement, we've prepared a 2025 timeline outlining our current plans for the development of the Beta throughout the year, keep in mind that this timeline may change over time as our situation changes or if we face challenges during development, the timeline is available right now on our website.

Reminder: You still have one day to get Park Studio 50% off!

Thank you all so much for your support, we cannot wait to share with you the very first Beta build of Park Studio, we are working very hard to provide the best game we can!

2025 will be a big year for us, and we hope we'll satisfy your expectations, stay tuned!

As always, we wish you all a great day! 🎢

In case you missed it: Take a look at our latest video showcasing our work in progress visual improvements for the game!

notes.title: Progress on the Beta 1.0 Graphics Improvements
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Azael here, I just wanted to quickly share some screenshots I took from previous saves with the improved lighting I've been working on the last few days.

Note: This announcement was first shared on the Discord, consider joining the community to discuss everything Park Studio: https://discord.gg/dbHc2mQWAz

I'm currently using Unreal Engine 5.5 with Mega-Lights, which uses Ray Traced shadows by default. These shadows can look worse than default shadows in some cases but they perform a tiny bit faster.

What has been improved? Mostly the lighting, Park Studio now uses what is called "PBL" or "Physically Based Lighting" which means I'm now using real values and proper post-processing to simulate what a camera would see. 

For example:

- What were previously fully-dark interiors are now properly lit when sunlight hits the interior.

- The sunlight now "burns" colors properly when hitting a surface directly.

- Materials are now rendered exactly how they should since Park Studio already used a PBR approach to materials (Physically Based Rendering)

Some other things have been tweaked such as the bloom method and lens flares, as well as the ambient fog for god rays.

This was a lot of fun to work on and I'm very happy with the results, this was a much needed improvement and I hope you'll all like it!

I cannot wait to share more information on the Beta! And stay tuned for an upcoming important announcement! 🎄

notes.title: The Future of the Park Studio Project
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

I'm Azael, and today I would like to give you some hopefully good news about the future of the Park Studio Project.

1. The plan for the future.

Park Studio's next release will be Beta 1.0, there is no release date for that update.

The goal is to provide an almost fully featured game in the far future instead of continuously creating small Alpha updates with bugged features that require complicated fixing. 

Targeting Beta will allow to re-create the entire game almost from the ground up in order to correct issues and improve the game with way more freedom, not having to worry about compatibility with Alpha.

This also means that Alpha saves will be entirely incompatible with the future Beta releases, since all of Park Studio's features will be reworked in some way.

2. Extending the audience of the game.

In order to be financially viable, the target audience of Park Studio will be extended to include casual players, a lot of features will be heavily simplified, while keeping advanced controls available for advanced players.

Here are a few major changes that are planned:

- The coaster builder will be reworked to be a lot simpler, with better controls and more visual helpers. The goal is to help casual players build nice and smooth coasters fast while advanced players will still be able to create near-perfect coasters by importing them from other software or using advanced controls like nodes. The current detailed systems will also be simplified such as special tracks, the goal being to provide pre-made sequences that are easy to edit for casual players, while advanced players will still be able to program their own sequences from scratch.

- The building system will be unified and simplified, Architecture and Scenery pieces will be merged in the same menu, and the Architecture pieces will be heavily simplified, the goal being to have one set of pieces with selectable sizes and materials instead of having 5000 pieces that are copies of each other with different materials.

- The UI and UX are going to be reworked, the UI will receive a fresh new look that will hopefully be easier on the eye, with a better font for reading. As for the UX improvements, there will be a lot of controls overhauls, and new camera controls for simulation enthusiasts that are used to "overview" cameras instead of the current first person camera.

This extenstion of the target audience is also to keep up with competition, the goal being to provide an alternative to popular games of the genre, with more customization, more realism, and more in-depth features for both casual and advanced players.

3. The Park Studio Experimental Branch.

An Experimental branch for Park Studio will soon be available for free on Steam, this Experimental branch will be updated each time a new system is done.

Saving in that branch will be disabled, in order to provide Patreon supporters with an advantage since that Experimental branch was previously private.

Patreon advantages will slightly change, you will still be able to access exclusive teasers and development insights and will get access to fully functional Experimental branch updates.

4. The Beta release.

As said previously, the Beta release currently doesn't have a release date, but you can expect it to release in 2025.

This Beta release will also come with a price increase, the game will jump from $14.99 USD to $19.99 USD and will exit Early Access.

After the Beta, only a few major features will be added before the game reaches full release and receives its first DLCs and Free Expansions.

5. Communication improvements

Communication about the development of the project will be improved, information will be provided on every platform and detailed devlogs are going to be created when relevant.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.2.0 (Phase 1) Release
notes.content:
Please note that while in its Alpha stage, we cannot guarantee Park Studio will work reliably on all hardware, please report any bugs or crashes you encounter. Bug reports will be fixed as soon as possible.

DISCLAIMER:

Alpha 0.2.0 is not the full "0.2" release, we are changing the way we release updates to provide more regular, feature rich updates. This means that an update such as 0.2 will be complete when all features are implemented via smaller updates. 0.2 is planned to be complete with 0.2.2!

Park Studio Alpha 0.2.0 has been released, here is what it currently includes:

- Coaster Builder Improvements: The coaster builder received a major upgrade, introducing a "Curve Tool" that allows for a better coaster building experience with automatic tangents! Nodes are still available for fine-tuning!

- Special Track Elements: Jump Tracks, Drop Tracks, Tilt Tracks and much more are waiting to be added to your coasters!

- Improved Coaster Physics: Coaster physics were drastically improved, and new customization options were added to control them further!

- Water Tools: Create Rivers around and in your parks! More water features such as lakes and oceans are coming soon!

- Foliage Painter: Using the brand new Foliage Painter, easily create forests or populate your park with grass, bushes and rocks!

- New Coaster Models: Go Beyond Vertical with the new Mug Rides LSM Launch Coaster "Comet", inspired by the Mack Rides Stryker Coaster, and soon, a brand new coaster type will turn your park upside down!

- CSV Track Importer: Import your coasters from other software directly in Park Studio using the CSV importer!

Coming next in Park Studio Alpha 0.2.1

Here are the features planned for release Alpha 0.2.1, coming soon.

- Additional Special Tracks: Switch Tracks, Transfer Tracks and other special tracks will come to complete the library of Special Tracks!

- New & Improved Water Tools: Water bodies will be added, along with a water shader overhaul allowing for better flowing water and scenery interactions!

- Prefabs & Steam Workshop: Prefabs will allow you to save your builds and share them on the Steam Workshop!

- Media Importer and Media Scenery: Screens, Flags, Speakers and more are coming to take your park to the next level with custom imported media!

- Menu Filters: Menu filters will come back to improve your experience when browsing the thousands of objects available in Park Studio!

- Track Components & Sounds: Better track components (LSM, Brakes) will come with sound and animations!

- Undo & Redo: Currently disabled in 0.2.0, Undo & Redo will come back in 0.2.1!

- Coaster Station Improvements: Coaster stations will be able to have a continuous movement, and trains will be able to open gates per row!

More features are planned to release in Alpha 0.2.2! Learn more on the trello.

CURRENT LIMITATIONS

- Special Tracks are still heavily Work In Progress, they are buggy especially with blocks, use with care.

- Special Track Elements cannot be inserted between nodes.

- Trains cannot go backwards with Special Track Elements, they will glitch out.

CHANGELOG

This update includes the following new features:

- New Camera Features: We added a few new Cinematic features to the Advanced Graphics Options, including color grading, depth of field, etc...

- Zoom: You can now Zoom using (C).

- POV Buttons on Train Cards: We added a few buttons to enter different camera positions on your trains via the Train Cards.

- Time Control: The Time and Weather Menu now includes new buttons to control time, you can slow down, stop or speed up time.

- New Upscaler : Nvidia DLSS 3.7 has been added, including DLSS, DLAA and NIS. (Note: Upscalers are not a solution to performance issues, they are only here to help with performance while we do our best to improve the game's bottlenecks.)

This update includes the following improvements:

- Massively Improved Performance: We optimized a lot of systems across the game, including lighting and materials and fixed some performance issues that were found before the initial release.

- Camera Speed and Mouse Sensitivity: You can now control the Flying and Walking camera speeds as well as the Mouse Sensitivity.

- Realistic Jump: We changed how the player character jumps, it should now be more realistic and less floaty.

- Menu Auto-Scaling: The Menus will now automatically scale up or down when you select/deselect an object or coaster, making it easier to browse the library while keeping viewport space when placing objects.

- Shader Pre-Compile Screen: We added a new Shader Compilation Screen when launching the game, this will compile all shaders allowing for a smoother game experience, you can disable the Pre-Compile Screen in the Options.

- New & Improved Main Menu: We improved the look and feel of the Main Menu.

- Interaction Crosshair: When in Walk Mode, if you look at an interactable object or coaster train, an interaction crosshair will appear indicating the object can be interacted with.

- Insert Node Improvements: When adding a node between two nodes, the new node will be inserted in the middle of the two others

- Arrive and Leave Tangents: Tangents are now separated between Arrive and Leave allowing for finer control over your curve's tangents.

- Auto Tangent Button: A new button to auto-calculate and apply tangents.

- Node Linking: Nodes can now be linked to each other, extending their settings without manual intervention.

- Snapping Improvements: Snapping can now snap to rotation and snap to scale.

- Hardware Ray Tracing Support: Support for Hardware Ray Tracing has been added, improving Ambient Occlusion, Reflections, Global Illumination and potentially improving performance on Ray Tracing capable graphic cards.

- Editable Coaster Friction: Coaster friction can be edited per coaster.

- Higher Resolution Terrain: Terrain resolution has been doubled, note that terrain paint may be reset.

- Units in Menus: Units are now displayed in Menus when needed.

- Longer Rain and Snow Coverage: Rain and Snow will last longer on the ground before melting or drying.

- New Terrain Textures: A few new terrain textures were added such as sand, leaves and gravel.

- New Foliage species: About a dozen new tree species were added including Pines, Palms, Oaks and more.

- Shadow Resolution Setting: A new setting that allows to control the "resolution" of shadows, this has very low impact on performance but can be useful.

Bug fixes:

- Nodes shouldn't reset colors anymore
- Grid Size can no longer be 0
- Decimals now display properly on supports settings
- All trains now have the same number of cars, name colors can still be adjusted per train
- Opening a closed loop coaster now removes the track components of the removed section
- Train audio issues were fixed
- The mouse should now be as responsive as your computer's mouse
- Park Name now saves and displays properly
- Opening the pause menu doesn't freeze the game
- Nodes can now be selected through terrain
- Node triggers were shortened to avoid overlapping track issues
- Fixed some typos
- The loading screen bar now displays 100% instead of 0% when loading has been completed

There are most probably more fixes that were forgotten, if issues persist, please report them again in the bug reports channel on the Discord.

Known Issues:

- Trains sometimes fold on themselves when switching from a Special Track to a normal track or when closing a coaster with a train on a special track or beyond.

- Blocks can bug with Special Tracks, they will not generate properly, especially with multiple Special Tracks.

- Closing a loop with Special Tracks currently only moves the last node to the first, this will be improved

notes.title: The Creye Games Patreon
notes.content:
We are opening a Patreon Page!

You can now support the development of the game by subscribing to a tier on our Patreon, more info below.

Why are we opening a Patreon?

As you may know, Park Studio has hit its sales goal, and has surpassed them since! But unfortunately, we did not correctly plan for the amount taxes and Steam would keep from those sales, which means we are currently unsure if the Park Studio project has the required funds to be developed to completion in a reasonable amount of time.

The cost of developing the game has also increased, we are needing more tools and more external support to surpass the challenges of using Unreal Engine 5, and create high quality content for you to enjoy, which is costly.

Adding to that, personal situation changes means life is costing more, and without an income, developing the Park Studio project full-time is not feasible.

That is why we are asking for your support, we are extremely thankful if you've purchased Park Studio and we know you are all waiting for more updates, new content and we will provide! We've made the promise to create an incredible game and we will respect this promise!

What are the tiers and advantages?

We are proposing 3 different tiers:

- Silver Supporter (1€ - 1,50$ USD): This tier supports us without any advantages, your name will be put on our website and in the game credits.

- Gold Supporter (5€ - 6$ USD) [**Recommended**]: This tier supports us and gives you access to exclusive teasers, early access to trailers, and exclusive game previews almost every week.

- Platinum Supporter (10€ - 11,50$ USD): This tier supports us and gives you access to all of the previous tier's advantages, plus free DLC content when DLCs come out (this tier currently does not offer anything more than the previous tier, but we appreciate your support!).

Does this mean updates will be locked behind a paywall?

No! The "Game Previews" that are proposed to Gold and Platinum Supporters are game builds that are very work in progress, some things may be broken or non-working. The updates will still release for free for everyone once the content is deemed ready!

You can access the Patreon Page by following this link

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.2 Development Update
notes.content:
Hello dear enthusiats!

Sorry for the lack of game updates, we've been working very hard on Alpha 0.2 and the tons of features it will add!

Here is a little update on what we've been working on, and what is left to do!

Alpha 0.2 Development

Development of the next big update has started after the last game update, Alpha 0.1.2, starting by adding a ton of Quality of Life features and upgrades such as a button on coasters to enter a train or new camera features such as Depth of Field, Zoom and more!

https://i.imgur.com/4PoBCQb.jpegScreenshot taken in-game using the new camera features

Then, the main menu and game UI was nearly entirely redone and improved to be more visually pleasing and performant.

https://i.imgur.com/4Bb9pqh.pngBrand new Main Menu

Speaking of performance, the game has received massive performance upgrades and fixes making the game run at a smooth 60 fps on the recommended configuration, on top of that, Nvidia DLSS support was added, including DLSS, DLAA, RTX Vibrance and Frame Generation.

After that, the focus was on entirely redoing the system that handles saving and loading your parks, a complicated and time consuming task that took nearly a month to complete due to unforseen issues and limitations. Thankfully, the system is now in place and allows us to add features without breaking your saves.

The next big feature was then implemented: Water!

Using the brand new Water Tools, you will be able to create next generation lakes, rivers and seas with ease. The tools use the same systems as the building and path tools, allowing you to place, move and scale water pieces to fit your needs, and use a spline-based river system similar to the game's Path Tool.

https://i.imgur.com/BbeHNqi.pngWIP screenshot of the early implementation of rivers

Developed along with the Water Tools, the Foliage Painter was also implemented and will allow you to paint foliage with fine controls!

Finally, the most recently implemented feature was the CSV track importer, allowing you to import track layouts from other popular softwares such as NoLimits 2, a great coaster simulation software, directly into Park Studio!

https://i.imgur.com/jJss42s.pngNoLimits2 coaster imported into Park Studio

And that's all we've been working on since June this year!

What is left to do

Before the update's release, there is still a few major features to implement, including:


 The brand new coaster elements, such as turn tables, switch tracks, drop tracks and more!
 Prefabs and the Steam Workshop allowing you to share your creations with the community!
 Custom Media using screens and speakers to make your park truly yours!


And the brand new Coaster Models, including the incredible Comet, that was recently revealed on our Discord

https://i.imgur.com/iV28knY.jpeg

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.2.D
notes.content:
This patch includes the following improvements:

- Collisions are a little bit more optimized.
- Lights are a little bit more optimized.

Bug fixes:

- Rocks, driftwood and logs now have collision.
- Hiding the UI and pausing should now shows the UI back, avoiding strange visibility behaviors.
- Selecting an Architecture object and then a Scenery object now clears the object description in the Object Selection panel.
- Stations should now work a little better, please note that spamming the state buttons can break the position of the train.
- Train colors should now load properly.
- Coasters will now update properly when inputting values in the transform panel.
- "Brake to Halt" doesn't reset the "Desired Speed" to 0 anymore.
- The Park Lamp will now turn off properly when darkening the light color.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.2.C
notes.content:
This patch includes the following improvements:

- The Move and Rotate gizmos will now hide the Axes that are not used when dragging.
- Duplicating a group will now create another group. A new group will be created as soon as one grouped object is duplicated.
- The range of scale for gizmos has been increased, gizmos will now scale smaller and bigger allowing for more precise and global edits.

Bug fixes:

- Unexpected track rotations should now be fixed.
- Setting the rotation from the rotation capsule should now work.
- Moving groups should now work properly.
- Rotating objects will not reset the scale.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.2.B
notes.content:
This patch includes the following improvements:

- Added a sound when successfuly duplicating objects.

Bug fixes:

- Cork Pieces will now display their material name properly.
- The scale button now works with coaster nodes.
- The weather sounds are now controlled by the ambience volume again.
- The rotation and scale gizmo won't have an audio glitch anymore.
- When pausing, the menu will go back to the main pause screen.
- When unpausing, the correct movement mode will be applied.
- The terrain brush will now only detect terrain.
- Clicking on an object through the interface is no longer possible.
- Rotating groups and using the rotation box on groups should now work.
- 4x4 Door Frames will now display the correct dimensions.
- The group ID will now update when grouping/ungrouping/disolving objects.
- The Reflection Quality slider will now work properly.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.2.A
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- The interface should now scale properly in windowed and windowed Fullscreen mode.
- Architecture pieces closely stacked together should stop glitching.
- Setting the tangents from a value in the Scale capsule should now work.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.2
notes.content:
We are now using Unreal Engine 5.4 and some new experimental features!

This update includes the following improvements:

- New and Revamped Architecture Pieces: We entirely revamped the way we handle the Architecture pieces internally. Note that this feature is experimental, it has a cost on performance that has not yet been fully tested, and can look worse than the old version of the Architecture pieces in some cases. We also added a few new shapes, sizes and materials.

IMPORTANT: Due to the new method we use to render Architecture Pieces, Architecture Pieces from previous versions will not load.


- New Look for the Menus: The menus received their new and improved look, the new design is more readable, more useable and should feel smoother than the previous version.

- New Main Menu Background: The office has been replaced with a brand new environment that is nicer and uses in-game pieces only.

- Coaster Supports: You will now find Coaster Supports pieces in the Building Menu.

- Primitives: New Primitive shapes will now be found in the building menu, those pieces are all kinds of shape and have flat plastic, stucco, metal and chrome textures.

- "Rain" is now "Light Rain" in the Weather Menu.

- The current Weather will now be outlined in the Weather Menu.

- When requesting a weather change, a pulsing outline will show around the desired weather until that weather is reached.

- Reduced manual Weather transition time.

- Keys that use CTRL or the Mouse Wheel now display the use of the combo in the Controls Options.

- Added Key Bindings for resetting the view in the coaster POVs (K), adding (SPACE) and removing (X) nodes.

- Clicking on nothing or miss-clicking will not close menus, to close menus you will now have to press MMB or ESC.

- You can now fine tune coaster tangents using the scale gizmo.

- Centered the spline of the track to the center of the mesh instead of the center of the spine. You will have to trigger a refresh for the supports.

- Added a toggleable flashlight (G).

- Added a key to hide the User Interface (H).

- Added a button to go back to the coaster base from the node menu.

Global Changes:

- The "Shadow Method" option has been removed as the "Low Quality" method is not compatible with the new features we are using in this update.

- Two options were added to toggle high-quality architecture pieces on and off as well as their scalability level.

- Filters have been temporarily removed, but you can type object attributes (Size, Material) in the search bar.

Bug fixes:

- Saves should now be safe when we change save data for options and parks.

- Snapping Architecture pieces at corners (90°) will now work.

- The save and load menus now have a scroll bar.

- Saving in the tutorial map is no longer possible.

- Interacting in Fly Mode is no longer possible.

- Pressing ESC when in the Pause Menu will now resume the game.

- The terrain brush is now clamped between 100 and 5000.

- The train's center of mass is now in the correct position.

- Adding a node will not reset the previous node's rotation.

- Paths should now rotate properly.

- The grid size will apply properly.

- Moving multiple coaster nodes at once  will regenerate the track on movement end.

- Doors and gates will stop glitching when being placed on an angle and opened.

Remaining Bugs & Known Issues:

- Architecture pieces look broken at the edges and corners, this is due to the workarounds we had to implement to use the new UE 5.4 experimental feature.

- Creating inversions is still broken.

- Performance of lighting and tracks is still bugged and will cause drastic frame rate drops.

- Blocks are bugged, creating coasters with multiple trains is not recommended.

- Undo & Redo is still heavily WIP and is mostly non-working.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1.E
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Adding a coaster node will not shift the previous node.
- Adding a coaster node will display the correct tangents.
- Changed the way coloring tracks work, recoloring the last node should now propagate the color to the next node properly, the color can then be edited for all the segments with the same color.
- Adding a node will not automatically disable the "Override Track Color", it should only be disabled when a node has changed color.
- Weather effects should now respect the "Ambient Volume" settings.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1.D
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Selecting Scenery objects will not automatically update attributes anymore.
- Duplicating lights will now correctly duplicate the attributes.
- Supports will regenerate correctly when resetting a node.
- Gizmos won't lock when leaving the pause menu.
- Fixed an issue with saves and coasters.

New!

- Added a Discord join button in the main menu.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1.C
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- The Rotation Gizmo will now disable the angles not supported by paths and coaster bases.
- The Scale Gizmo will no longer take the rotation of the object.
- Disabled the Camera movement in the menu after sickness reports.
- Paths won't scale on the Z axis when inputting scale from the menu.
- Duplicating objects should now always work.
- Duplicating path nodes, coaster nodes and coaster bases has been disabled.
- Setting Transforms from the Transform Capsule will now work on multi-selections.
- Tracks won't randomly change color when deleting a specific type of track and adding a new node right after.
- More rotation issues with the tracks and saving rotations should now work as intended.
- Rotating multi-selected objects will not be multiplied by the number of objects anymore.

CRITICAL KNOWN ISSUE:

- Rotating multi-selections on more than one axis causes wrong rotations for all the selected objects except the pivot. This bug will be fixed as soon as possible.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1.B
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Adding a new coaster node will not shift the rotation of all nodes anymore.
- Adding/Removing cars will now stop the audio correctly
- Changed the range of middle cars to 1 - 20 (previously 0 - 10)

Switched to Unreal Engine 5.4, expect better overall performance and quality, and possible issues while we fully test the game in the new version of the engine.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1.A
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Load tiles that have an invalid thumbnail will now have the correct color for the hover and click outline.
- The hanging lantern now produces light.
- Track rotation issues have been fixed.

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.1
notes.content:
This update includes the following improvements:

- Coaster bases are now a little bit longer.
- The right side of the coaster editor is now a little wider, to make space for the new "Tangent Size".
- The new "Tangent Size" (Tightness) has been improved, the range is now from 1 to 10 000 (previously 0 - 4000), making it easier to smooth large elements (especially useful for Hyper / Giga coasters).
- A new tangent visualizer has been added to coaster nodes, it should help making smooth curves easier. The visualizer can be disabled in the gameplay options.
- The default values for stations, launches, brakes, etc are now different based on real life observations.
- Multiple coaster nodes can now be edited at once, coaster nodes will also change color when selected.
- Resetting a node now resets the tangents on top of resetting its rotation.
- Trains will now reset to a block when closing coasters.
- Camera Collision in fly mode can now be disabled in the options.
- A new filter section has been added to the side of the Scenery menu, the same filter section will be added to more menus later on.
- Track components will now generate without gaps between nodes.
- Stations now generate the components related to the "Dispatch Device".
- The tutorial has been entirely revamped, it is now visual and interactive.
- Removed the block condition for spawning trains, trains can now be added to single-block coasters.

Bug fixes:

- The Path and Coaster node's arrows will now use the selection color instead of red when selected.
- Removed the track in the background of the Main Menu as it caused performance issues in the menu.
- Trains now despawn when deleting a coaster. Note: When undoing, the train will not be spawned back.
- Loading a coaster now loads the correct data for each node.
- Tire wheels now display with correct texture and color.

IMPORTANT NOTE: While the coaster editor is extremely flexible, some angles or combination of angle and tangent can cause the track to drastically deform and potentially break your coaster. We recommend editing the track at a slow pace and to only build feasible layouts. As a reminder, Park Studio is not a fantasy game, so building things that wouldn't exist in the real world will cause issues, and will not be regarded as bugs.

We are currently working on a video tutorial series that will cover the systems of Park Studio from basic to advanced, if you have ideas for what should be covered in this series, please tell us in our Discord!

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.0.C
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Undoing and Redoing actions related to the coaster editor and path editor should now be fixed.
- Track components (LSM fins, brakes, etc) now generate with a smaller gap in between sections.
- Setting the time of day below midnight doesn't crash the game anymore.
- Placing an object with the height shortcut, closing the menu and trying to place a new object doesn't freeze the object anymore.
- Height will not reset when releasing the height Key anymore (SHIFT by Default).
- Menus will now remember if you had a tab selected or if you had a search text inputted.
- "Tightness" has been renamed "Tangents Size" in preparation for 0.1.1.
- "Track Colors" is now in bold to fit with the rest of the track menu.
- "Disptach Interval" is now "Dispatch Interval".

The next Update, 0.1.1, will focus on improving the coaster editor and the tutorials available in the game as well as some improvements to the menus.

Thanks to everyone who reported bugs!

Have a great day! 🎢

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1.0.B
notes.content:
This patch includes the following bug fixes:

- Gizmos are now easier to select, they also got a new look.
- The sliders in the transform capsule have been disabled, you can now only type values in the capsules.
- Coaster Nodes are now a little bit bigger and easier to select, previously they were too small and the game selected the track instead.
- Inserting a node between two nodes doesn't make the track disappear.

Known issues:

- The Undo and Redo causes many issues with the coaster and path system, those issues will be fixed in the next patch. For now we advise you not to use the Undo and Redo system with coasters and paths.

If you are encountering any issues while playing Park Studio, please report them in our Discord, there is a new channel to give your feedback for the game as well.

We will soon begin development on Alpha 0.2, which means we won't be able to produce patches for Alpha 0.1, so please report all the bugs you encounter so we can fix them now. Thank you.

Have a great day! 🎢

notes.title: Park Studio Alpha 0.1 has been released!
notes.content:
Please note that while in its Alpha stage, we cannot guarantee Park Studio will work reliably on all hardware, please report any bugs or crashes on our Discord server. Bug reports will be fixed as soon as possible.

Park Studio Alpha 0.1 has been released, here is what it includes:

- The Coaster Editor : A tool that allows you to build awesome roller coasters with many customization options. In this release, the editor comes with 3 highly detailed coaster models, as well as basic coaster track editing.

- The Park Building Tools : The base of the game, the building tools allow you to place and edit architecture and scenery pieces in your park. This release includes over 3000+ architecture and scenery pieces to play with. (Most pieces are placeholders, they are using bought assets from the Unreal Engine Marketplace and will be replaced in a future release with higher quality models). Note: The Undo and Redo systems are WIP, some actions are not yet supported, be careful when building.

- The Path Editor : A tool that allows you to build paths allowing your visitors (coming soon) to go around your park and enjoy your creations. This release comes with a a few path textures and customization options.

- Terrain Editing : A set of tools that allow you to sculpt the terrain of your park to your liking. This release comes with over a few terrain textures to adjust the look and feel of your landscapes.

Coming soon in Park Studio Alpha 0.2

Here are the features planned for release Alpha 0.2, coming soon.

- Water body generation : A set of tools that will allow you to create lakes and flowing rivers.

- New Coaster Types : Two new coaster types will join the 3 already included.

- Transfer Tracks & Special Elements : An addition to the Coaster Editor, allowing you to build more complex rides with quick switch tracks, turn tables and more.

- Better Sounds & Music : Due to the small budget we had for the first release of the game we couldn't get our hands on the sounds and music we wanted, the sounds of the game will progressively be upgraded update after update (Note: Some objects or rides may have no sound in Alpha 0.1).

There is still a lot of features planned for releases after the Alpha, you can find a brief summary of those features on our website here.

Important Note: Park Studio Alpha 0.1 is a "proof of concept" release that is only meant to showcase the base idea for the game, the goal of this release is to fund the project and allow it progress and evolve, you can participate in the funding of the game by inviting your friends to purchase and play Park Studio. Due to the game being in a very early stage of development, we highly encourage you not to play the game too seriously, we would advise not to start mega projects as the game can drastically change in future releases. Instead, we advise you to enjoy the features currently available and give us feedback!
